n0c95fece71e.s: Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary is located in which State?
n0c95fece71e.x: Ranganathittu is on Kaveri islets in Mandya, Karnataka.

nindian-geography-42-6.s: Bharatpur (Keoladeo) Bird Sanctuary is located in which State?
nindian-geography-42-6.x: Bharatpur (Keoladeo) is in Rajasthan, not Haryana; Sultanpur is the Haryana sanctuary.

nenvironment-18-2.s: Parvati Arga Bird Sanctuary is located in which district?
nenvironment-18-2.x: Parvati Arga is in Gonda, Uttar Pradesh; Sahibganj (Jharkhand) has Udhwa, Unnao has Nawabganj and Rae Bareli has Samaspur.

n8b657301478.s: Which bird breeds on high Central Asian lakes and crosses the Himalaya to winter in India?
n8b657301478.x: The Bar-headed goose, one of the highest-flying birds, crosses the Himalaya to winter in India. The Amur falcon winters in southern Africa.

ncd150836c0e.s: Gir, the only natural home of the Asiatic lion, is in which State?
ncd150836c0e.x: Gir is in Gujarat. Bhitarkanika and Gahirmatha are the Odisha sites.

nce701138deb.s: How many major soil types are recognised in India's classification?
nce701138deb.x: Eight: alluvial, black, red and yellow, laterite, arid, saline and alkaline, peaty and marshy, and forest and mountain soils.

nindian-geography-19-6.s: Laterite soil in India occurs mainly on the:
o: Summits of the Western and Eastern Ghats
nindian-geography-19-6.x: Laterite soil occurs on the summits of the Western and Eastern Ghats; the Northern Plains have alluvial, the Deccan lava plateau black and the crystalline Peninsula red soil.

nindian-geography-19-2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the alluvial belts of the northern plains?
o: Khadar is new alluvium deposited by floods
Bhabar is a marshy lowland lying south of the Tarai
Bhangar is old alluvium on higher ground beyond normal flood reach
Streams sink and disappear in the pebbly Bhabar belt
nindian-geography-19-2.x: Bhabar is the pebbly foothill belt where streams sink; the marshy Tarai lies south of it, not the other way round.

n4ea8f02abba.s: Which rainfall factor generally matters more for the rate of soil erosion?
n4ea8f02abba.x: Rainfall intensity generally matters more than total annual rainfall for soil erosion.

na9f78d48b87.s: Which soil-conservation measure traps sediment and checks gully growth?
na9f78d48b87.x: Check dams trap sediment and check gully growth; shelter belts are tree rows that cut wind speed.

n868bb13c8a4.s: The Archaean and Dharwar rocks of India are chiefly known for:
n868bb13c8a4.x: Archaean and Dharwar rocks hold metallic minerals. Gondwana rocks hold coal, Tertiary rocks petroleum and Cuddapah rocks barytes and asbestos.

nindian-geography-43-12.s: Which rock system forms India's oldest metamorphic schist belts, rich in iron ore and gold?
nindian-geography-43-12.x: The Dharwar system forms the oldest schist belts; Gondwana rocks lie in the Damodar, Son, Mahanadi and Godavari basins.

nchemistry-3-73.s: Na₃AlF₆ is the chemical formula of:
nchemistry-3-73.x: Cryolite is Na₃AlF₆. Ilmenite is FeTiO₃, corundum is anhydrous Al₂O₃ and bauxite is Al₂O₃·xH₂O.

nb925cc134cd.s: Balaghat and Chhindwara in Madhya Pradesh are important areas of which mineral?
nb925cc134cd.x: Balaghat and Chhindwara are manganese-bearing areas of Madhya Pradesh, as Sundargarh and Kendujhar are in Odisha.

nap-geography-6-12.s: Bethamcherla and Koilakuntla in Kurnool district are major centres of:
nap-geography-6-12.x: Bethamcherla and Koilakuntla are the main limestone centres; barytes is linked to the Kadapa rocks.

new.s: The Ramsar Convention of 1971 concerns the conservation and wise use of:
new.x: The Ramsar Convention, adopted at Ramsar, Iran, in 1971, is for the conservation and wise use of wetlands.

new.s: India became a party to the Ramsar Convention in:
new.x: India joined in 1982; the Convention was adopted in 1971 and Chilika was designated in 1981.

new.s: Under the Ramsar definition, a wetland includes marine water up to what depth at low tide?
new.x: Ramsar wetlands include marine water up to 6 m deep at low tide, and may be natural or artificial.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Ramsar Convention?
o: It was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran
World Wetlands Day is observed on 22 March
Artificial water bodies can qualify as wetlands
Keoladeo and Loktak are India's Montreux Record sites
new.x: World Wetlands Day is 2 February; 22 March is World Water Day.

new.s: Which wetland became India's 100th Ramsar site on 5 June 2026?
new.x: Surha Tal (JP Narayan Bird Sanctuary), Ballia, UP, was the 100th; Shekha Jheel was 99th and Glaw Lake 101st.

new.s: Shekha Jheel, India's 99th Ramsar site (April 2026), is in which State?
new.x: Shekha Jheel Bird Sanctuary in Uttar Pradesh became the 99th Ramsar site in April 2026.

new.s: Sasthamkotta Ramsar site is in which State?
new.x: Sasthamkotta is in Kerala, not Tamil Nadu.

new.s: Which Ramsar site is wrongly matched with its State?
new.x: Menar, added in 2025, is in Rajasthan; the other pairs are correct.

new.s: Glaw Lake, Arunachal Pradesh's first Ramsar site, lies inside which tiger reserve?
new.x: Glaw Lake, India's 101st Ramsar site (Aug 2026), lies inside Kamlang Tiger Reserve and is home to the white-bellied heron.

new.s: Project Tiger was launched on 1 April 1973 with how many reserves?
new.x: Project Tiger began in 1973 with 9 reserves.

new.s: The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), a statutory body, was set up in:
new.x: NTCA was set up in 2006 under the amended Wildlife (Protection) Act.

new.s: M-STrIPES, used in India's tiger reserves, is:
o: An app-based patrolling and monitoring tool
new.x: M-STrIPES is an app-based patrolling and monitoring tool used in tiger reserves.

new.s: According to the All India Tiger Estimation 2022, India's average tiger count was:
new.x: AITE 2022 gave an average of 3,682 tigers; 1,411 was the 2006 baseline.

new.s: Which is India's first tiger reserve, where Project Tiger was formally launched in 1973?
new.x: Project Tiger was formally launched at Corbett, India's first tiger reserve (1973).

new.s: Which tiger reserve is wrongly matched with its State?
new.x: Buxa is in West Bengal (Alipurduar); Odisha's tiger reserve in the list is Satkosia.

new.s: Madhav, India's 58th tiger reserve (March 2025), is in which State?
new.x: Madhav in Madhya Pradesh became the 58th tiger reserve in March 2025.

new.s: Amangarh Tiger Reserve, a buffer of Corbett, lies in which State?
new.x: Amangarh is in Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh, as a buffer of Corbett.

new.s: Which is India's largest tiger reserve?
new.x: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam (AP) is the largest; Guru Ghasidas-Tamor Pingla is third after NSTR and Manas.

new.s: India's elephant reserves, spread over 14 States, number:
new.x: There are 33 elephant reserves in 14 States under Project Elephant (1992).

new.s: Which two States have the most elephant reserves, five each?
new.x: Assam and Tamil Nadu have 5 elephant reserves each; Odisha has 3.

new.s: According to the DNA-based census of October 2025, which State has the largest wild elephant population?
new.x: The census counted 22,446 wild elephants, with Karnataka having the largest population.

new.s: Bhitarkanika in Odisha is known chiefly for:
new.x: Bhitarkanika is known for saltwater crocodiles and mangroves; olive ridley nesting is at Gahirmatha.

new.s: The National Chambal Sanctuary chiefly protects the:
new.x: National Chambal (Rajasthan–MP–UP) protects the gharial and the Gangetic dolphin.

new.s: During its migration, the Amur falcon makes a stopover in October-November in:
new.x: Amur falcons stop over in Nagaland (Doyang, Pangti) on their way to winter in southern Africa.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's only tiger reserve is:
new.x: AP has only one tiger reserve, NSTR; Rayala is its elephant reserve.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the five factors of soil formation?
new.x: The five factors are parent material, climate, relief, organisms and time; soil colour is a property, not a factor.

new.s: Limestone giving rise to calcium-rich soil shows the influence of which soil-formation factor?
new.x: Parent rock passes on its traits, e.g. limestone gives calcium-rich soil.

new.s: India's average soil organic carbon reportedly fell over 70 years from 1% to:
new.x: India's average SOC reportedly fell from 1% to 0.3% over 70 years.

new.s: Which soil is the most widespread in India, covering about 45.6% of its area?
new.x: Alluvial soil covers about 15 lakh sq km (45.6%), the most widespread.

new.s: Black (regur) soil contains clay of more than:
new.x: Black soil has more than 62% clay, giving it the highest moisture retention.

new.s: Red and yellow soil looks yellow when its iron oxide is:
new.x: The red colour comes from iron oxide; it turns yellow when hydrated.

new.s: Kankar (calcareous concretions) is characteristic of:
new.x: Kankar belongs to Bhangar, the old alluvium; the claim that Khadar holds calcareous deposits is false.

new.s: Karewa soils of the Kashmir Valley are:
new.x: Karewas are lacustrine deposits of gravel and mud on plateaus above the Jhelum plains.

new.s: Laterite soil of Andhra Pradesh is notably poor in:
new.x: Laterite is poor in nitrogen but has excess iron oxide and potash; 'N is plentiful in AP laterite' is wrong.

new.s: Which Indian soil is rich in phosphorus?
new.x: Desert soil, though poor in nitrogen and humus, is rich in phosphorus; black, red and laterite soils are poor in it.

new.s: Peaty soils form in areas of:
o: Heavy rainfall, high humidity and good vegetation
Low rainfall over granite and gneiss
new.x: Peaty soils form where heavy rain, humidity and vegetation let organic matter build faster than it rots; semi-arid salinity describes saline soil.

new.s: Which Indian soil has the highest moisture retention?
new.x: Black soil, with over 62% clay, has the highest moisture retention.

new.s: Which is the smallest soil order in India?
new.x: Mollisols are India's smallest soil order; Inceptisols are the largest.

new.s: In the ICAR/USDA classification, Vertisols correspond to which Indian soil?
new.x: Vertisols are the black soils, covering about 8.5% of India.

new.s: Which type of soil erosion is widespread but the least noticed?
new.x: Sheet erosion removes a thin uniform topsoil layer and is the least noticed; gully erosion is the final stage.

new.s: Which is the most powerful agent of soil erosion?
new.x: Water is the most powerful erosion agent.

new.s: Biochar added to soil reportedly cuts soil nitrous oxide emissions by about:
new.x: Biochar raises water holding and cuts soil N2O by about 30–50%.

new.s: Which cause of land degradation is correctly matched with the States it affects?
new.x: Overgrazing affects Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP and Maharashtra; over-irrigation Punjab, Haryana and western UP; mining Jharkhand, Odisha, MP and Chhattisgarh.

new.s: The Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas of June 2021 was prepared by:
new.x: The atlas was prepared by ISRO's Space Applications Centre (SAC), Ahmedabad.

new.s: As per the 2021 Desertification Atlas, what share of India's land was degraded in 2018-19?
new.x: About 97.85 mha (29.7%) was degraded in 2018-19, up from 28.76% in 2003-05.

new.s: Soil Health Cards are issued to farmers once every:
new.x: Soil Health Cards are issued every two years and test 12 parameters.

new.s: Which State had issued the most Soil Health Cards as of February 2026?
new.x: Of 25.79 crore cards generated by February 2026, Uttar Pradesh issued the most.

new.s: Which series forms the Lower Vindhyan system?
new.x: Semri is the Lower Vindhyan; Kaimur, Rewa and Bhander make up the Upper Vindhyan.

new.s: Coal, gypsum, salt and potash typically occur as:
new.x: Coal, gypsum, salt and potash occur in sedimentary beds; placers hold gold, tin and platinum.

new.s: Malachite is an ore of:
new.x: Malachite, Cu₂(CO₃)(OH)₂, is a copper ore; zinc is from zinc blende, mercury from cinnabar, manganese from pyrolusite.

new.s: Cassiterite (SnO₂) is an ore of:
new.x: Cassiterite is the ore of tin; tungsten is from wolframite, titanium from ilmenite and rutile, thorium from monazite.

new.s: Sukinda in Odisha is famous for:
new.x: Sukinda in Odisha is India's noted chromite area.

new.s: The Kudremukh iron-ore deposits of Karnataka are in which district?
new.x: Kudremukh is in Chikkamagaluru district.

new.s: Bhandara is a manganese-producing district of which State?
new.x: Bhandara is the manganese area of Maharashtra.

new.s: Which is the only tin-producing State of India?
new.x: Chhattisgarh (Dantewada) is the only tin producer, though Haryana holds the larger share of resources.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Rajasthan's minerals?
o: It is the sole producer of lead-zinc ores
Zawar near Udaipur is a lead-zinc area
It is the sole producer of copper ore
Khetri in Jhunjhunu is a copper area
new.x: Rajasthan is the sole lead-zinc producer, not the sole copper producer; MP ranks first in copper ore.

new.s: Lohardaga in Jharkhand is an important area of:
new.x: Lohardaga is Jharkhand's bauxite area; Jaduguda and Turamdih are uranium.

new.s: Koderma in Jharkhand is known for:
new.x: Koderma lies in the Koderma–Gaya–Hazaribagh–Munger mica belt.

new.s: Lapsa Buru in Jharkhand is known for which refractory mineral?
new.x: Kyanite occurs at Lapsa Buru; sillimanite at Sona Pahar (Meghalaya).

new.s: Makrana in Rajasthan is famous for:
new.x: Makrana marble was used in the Taj Mahal and Victoria Memorial; salt comes from Didwana.

new.s: Gypsum, used in cement, fertiliser and plaster, comes chiefly from:
new.x: Rajasthan is the main gypsum area.

new.s: Barytes is used mainly in:
new.x: Barytes is used in oil-well drilling mud; asbestos for fire-proofing, kyanite for refractories, dolomite as steel flux.

new.s: In 2024-25, which State ranked second after Odisha in the value of mineral production?
new.x: The 2024-25 order was Odisha > Rajasthan > Chhattisgarh > Karnataka > Maharashtra.

new.s: India produces how many minerals?
new.x: India produces 95 minerals: 4 fuel, 10 metallic, 23 non-metallic, 3 atomic and 55 minor.

new.s: In February 2023, GSI reported 5.9 million tonnes of inferred lithium at Salal-Haimana in which district?
new.x: The lithium find was at Salal-Haimana, Reasi (J&K); its auction was annulled for want of bids.

new.s: The National Critical Mineral Mission aims to acquire how many overseas mineral assets?
new.x: NCMM targets 50 overseas assets, 1,200 exploration projects by 2030-31 and 15+ critical minerals.

new.s: Rare earths comprise how many elements?
new.x: Rare earths are 17 elements; China accounts for about 70% of their mining.

new.s: Under the MMDR Act, 1957, minor minerals are regulated by:
new.x: Minor minerals are with the States (Section 15); major minerals are with the Centre.
